title: Cohort Science™ Introduces Education Outcomes Platform™ for Institutional Leaders to Measure Education Outcomes and Mobility
excerpt: Cohort Science™ announced findings from its Education Outcomes Platform™, showing how community college and university credentials translate into measurable economic outcomes and mobility.
author: Cohort Science™
content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Cohort Science™ Introduces Education Outcomes Platform™ for Institutional Leaders to Measure Education Outcomes and Mobility

Multi-year view of cohort education outcomes trends and insights for institutional leaders, delivered at decision speed — revealing which student behaviors predict career outcomes and where graduates actually build their careers.

Dallas, TX — July 2, 2026 — Cohort Science™ today announced the release of its findings on how community college and university credentials translate into real-world economic outcomes.

The analysis, produced using the company’s Education Outcomes Platform™, segments graduate cohorts across many dimensions, including academic, demographic, and psychographic. For institutional leaders and stakeholders, the platform renders clear, powerful, and actionable insights into career mobility across salary, seniority, geography, and industry over a multi-year post-graduation window. For institutions, the platform provides trustable data and insights to demonstrate the institution’s true impact on lives.

Every college claims to change lives. Few can prove it with data.

The results challenge long-standing assumptions in academic advising — and surface signals that institutional leaders and impact investors into the sector have not had access to before, far faster than conventional outcomes research allows.

“In today’s world, the key institutional decisions pertaining to the foundational E’s — enrollments, equity, and endowments — all depend on demonstrating outcomes. Our Education Outcomes Platform™ is built to address exactly this need: powerful, decision-ready insights into your institution’s specific impact.”

— Lauren Jensen, Partner, Cohort Science

The challenge is not intent — it is access. The data required to answer the most important question — did this degree improve this student’s economic trajectory? — exists in fragments: market demand signals, salary trends, career growth patterns, geographic shifts, and industry mobility that institutions cannot easily connect. Education Outcomes Platform™ unifies these sources into a single, continuous measurement system that finally makes the full post-graduation picture visible.

Why this matters

The scrutiny of higher education’s value continues to intensify, as questions about the ROI of a credential become central to public, institutional, and policy conversations. Institutional leaders face growing pressure to demonstrate outcomes with data and evidence. Traditional metrics such as graduation rates and job placement offer only partial insight. The gap shows up in building reliable longitudinal trends of cohort outcomes and mobility.

Economic mobility — the measurable progress a student achieves over time in salary, seniority, and career trajectory — is the true outcome. Education Outcomes Platform™ is designed to measure this at the level of individual student behavior, continuously, across an institution’s full graduate population.

About Education Outcomes Platform™

Education Outcomes Platform™ is Cohort Science’s SaaS platform for measuring post-graduation economic outcomes. It segments graduates by behavioral patterns and graduation cohorts, then tracks their careers across five key dimensions:

  • Economic mobility — seniority progression, salary growth, and time-to-milestone across configurable post-graduation windows.
  • Job outcomes — time-to-first-job, entry role composition, and long-term earnings paths.
  • Geographic flow — where graduates work, which cities retain talent, and which roles migrate.
  • Industry trajectory — how graduates move across industries and role categories over time.
  • Price-to-outcome alignment — net price paid per cohort against realized labor market value of the credential, the first view that lets institutions and analysts evaluate revenue and outcome on the same students.

Together, these dimensions make visible patterns of mobility, retention, and program value that are difficult to see in standard enrollment or outcomes reports.

Education sector leaders and impact investors rely on the platform for high quality, predictive insights into mobility and workforce trends. Education Outcomes Platform™ delivers powerful data and decision-ready insights to measure institution-specific outcomes and mobility. Subscription access is available at Early-Partner Pricing upon request.

Insights are delivered through interactive reporting designed for presidents, provosts, and governing boards, as well as analysts and stakeholders invested in the sector.

Years of quiet work. One platform. A new answer to the question every institution should already be answering.

About Cohort Science

Cohort Science™ is a higher education-focused data science and institutional intelligence firm. The company helps colleges and universities strengthen enrollment, retention, operational performance, academic portfolio strategy, and graduate outcomes through advanced analytics and independent evaluation frameworks.

The Great Divergence in Higher Education: Cohort Science™ Unveils Investor-Grade Institutional Intelligence Platform

New strategic intelligence suite helps colleges and universities strengthen enrollment, financial sustainability, workforce alignment, and institutional performance during a period of growing institutional separation

DALLAS, TX — 7 May 2026 — Higher education is entering what many institutional leaders increasingly recognize as a period of “The Great Divergence” — a widening separation between institutions operating with real-time market intelligence, operational discipline, and workforce alignment and those continuing to rely primarily on legacy assumptions and fragmented decision-making processes.

In response to this shift, Cohort Science today announced the launch of its integrated institutional intelligence platform designed specifically to help colleges and universities navigate rising enrollment pressures, demographic change, financial complexity, shifting workforce demands, and growing scrutiny around institutional value and student outcomes.

The Cohort Science platform combines market analysis, student outcomes intelligence, strategic planning support, and institutional performance evaluation into a unified decision-support framework built for presidents, provosts, CFOs, governing boards, and enrollment leaders.

“The Great Divergence is not simply about enrollment decline or demographic pressure,” said Raj Lalsare, Founder and CEO at Cohort Science. “It reflects a broader separation between institutions that can rapidly align programs, operations, pricing, and student outcomes with market realities and those struggling to adapt with sufficient speed and clarity. Our goal is to help institutional leaders navigate that transition with confidence.”

Cohort Science Strategic Intelligence Suite™

The Cohort Science Strategic Intelligence Suite™ was developed to help institutions move beyond static reporting and reactive management toward more predictive, evidence-based institutional leadership.

The platform is organized around four integrated strategic intelligence areas designed to help institutions strengthen both mission impact and long-term sustainability during a period of accelerating sector transformation.

CS MarketSignal™

CS MarketSignal™ is a market intelligence and academic portfolio evaluation framework designed to help institutions assess program viability, workforce demand, pricing strategy, competitive positioning, and enrollment opportunity before making significant investment decisions.

As institutions increasingly compete for a smaller and more discerning student population, the platform helps leadership teams identify where genuine market opportunity exists — and where institutional resources may be better redeployed.

The solution synthesizes labor market trends, student demand indicators, competitive conditions, institutional fit, regional dynamics, and economic mobility data into a comprehensive strategic analysis framework.

Dean’s Workbench™ by Cohort Science

Dean’s Workbench™ provides academic leaders with a strategic planning and operational performance environment focused on enrollment management, student retention, resource allocation, and academic program optimization.

In an era where operational efficiency and student persistence are becoming increasingly tied to institutional sustainability, the platform enables institutions to evaluate trends, model intervention strategies, and better align operational decisions with institutional priorities and student success objectives.

CS Vector™

Vector™ is a student outcomes and economic mobility intelligence solution designed to help institutions better understand graduate outcomes, workforce alignment, salary trajectories, geographic mobility, and long-term student value.

As public scrutiny around higher education return on investment continues to increase, the platform provides evidence-based insights that support accreditation reporting, fundraising initiatives, employer partnerships, academic planning, and student recruitment efforts.

CS ImpactAudit™

CS ImpactAudit™ is an independent institutional evaluation framework designed to assess the effectiveness and return on investment of academic programs, strategic initiatives, grants, partnerships, departments, and operational functions.

At a time when institutional leaders and governing boards face increasing pressure to demonstrate measurable impact and operational accountability, the framework provides objective analysis to support resource allocation decisions, strategic planning, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Moving From Reactive Management to Strategic Visibility

Cohort Science was founded on the belief that higher education institutions require more than dashboards and static reporting tools. They require trusted analytical partners capable of transforming complex institutional and market data into actionable strategic insight.

The company’s work supports institutions seeking to improve enrollment growth, operational effectiveness, student retention, workforce alignment, academic portfolio strategy, and long-term institutional sustainability.

“Our role is not simply to provide data,” Lalsare added. “It is to help institutional leaders gain greater visibility into the forces shaping higher education so they can make better decisions earlier and lead their institutions proactively rather than reactively.”

About Cohort Science

Cohort Science is a higher education-focused data science and institutional intelligence firm that helps colleges and universities improve enrollment, retention, operational performance, academic portfolio strategy, and student outcomes through advanced analytics and strategic evaluation frameworks.

By transforming complex institutional and market data into actionable insights, Cohort Science helps institutional leaders strengthen both mission impact and financial sustainability in an increasingly competitive higher education environment.

For more information, visit cohortscience.com

title: Cohort Science Announces Market Analysis Platform to Help Universities Evaluate New Program Opportunities
excerpt: DALLAS, TX, [April 29, 2026] — Cohort Science today announced the launch of its Market SignalAnalysis Platform, a decision-support solution designed to help colleges and universities evaluatenew academic program opportun
content:
DALLAS, TX, [April 29, 2026] — Cohort Science today announced the launch of its Market Signal
Analysis Platform, a decision-support solution designed to help colleges and universities evaluate
new academic program opportunities with greater clarity and confidence.

The platform integrates four core pillars of academic program success—labor market demand,
student demand, career value, and competitive conditions—alongside institution-specific variables
such as faith-based market positioning, faculty strength, brand equity, and strategic mission
alignment. Together, these inputs form a unified framework for evaluating program viability and
growth potential.

Developed through applied work with multiple institutions, the framework has been used to assess
opportunities across multiple disciplines. The analysis provides key regional trends across multiple
stated by comparing program completions, competitive positioning, tuition levels, job openings,
median wages, and delivery formats such as online and hybrid.

The platform is designed for institutional leaders facing critical questions:

  • Is this program opportunity viable?
  • How can an existing program become more competitive?
  • Where is there meaningful room for growth?

Rather than relying on a single data source or static report, Cohort Science combines multiple
market signals into a unified model that enables leaders to evaluate demand, competitive intensity,
and strategic fit more holistically.

Cohort Science’s approach includes both analytical and visual components that help institutions
move from raw data to action. The platform includes a scoring model that assigns each program a
composite score based on market conditions, alongside intuitive visualizations that compare
opportunity across regions. This approach helped identify high-potential program opportunities and
clarified where institutional investment would drive the strongest returns.

With this launch, Cohort Science is introducing a standardized, repeatable platform for academic
market intelligence—particularly valuable for institutions evaluating new programs in healthcare,
social sciences, business, and other workforce-aligned fields. The platform supports use cases
ranging from new program discovery to repositioning existing offerings for stronger growth and
long-term sustainability.

Institutions interested in learning more or participating in early engagements can reach us at
www.cohortscience.com

title: Kentucky Christian University Selects Cohort Science for Online Expansion Strategy
excerpt: Richardson, TX — December 19, 2025 — Kentucky Christian University (KCU) has entered into a new agreement with Cohort Science to support online expansion with data-driven insights for enrollment growth and market positioning.
content:
Richardson, TX — December 19, 2025 — Kentucky Christian University (KCU) has entered into a new agreement with Cohort Science, a higher education data science firm specializing in using data to help colleges and universities improve enrollment, retention, and student satisfaction. The collaboration will support KCU’s online expansion strategy and provide the institution with the data-driven insights necessary to increase online enrollment and strengthen its competitive position across faith-centered higher education markets.

Under the new agreement, Cohort Science will conduct a holistic evaluation of both new and existing academic programs. The project encompasses an integrated assessment of program demand, labor-market alignment, competitor offerings, student decision behaviors, geographic opportunity, brand perception, and price-sensitivity indicators. This unified approach will give KCU a comprehensive understanding of where the strongest opportunities exist to grow and sustain new and existing online degree programs.

Raj Lalsare, Founder and CEO of Cohort Science, emphasized the alignment between the two organizations, noting: “We are honored to support Kentucky Christian University in advancing its mission to develop Christian leaders grounded in faith, service, and academic excellence. KCU’s commitment to stewardship and intentional, data-driven decision-making aligns beautifully with our purpose at Cohort Science. By integrating longitudinal analysis, market intelligence, and missional context, we look forward to helping KCU grow new and existing programs.”

KCU’s new initiative comes at a time of increased demand for high-quality online programs—especially those rooted in Christian worldview and service leadership. As part of this engagement, Cohort Science will conduct scorecard-based evaluations of selected new and existing programs.

Reflecting on the University’s goals, John Penrose, Vice President of Enrollment and Marketing at Kentucky Christian University, highlighted the strategic significance of the partnership: “KCU is committed to expanding access to high-quality, Christ-centered academic programs, especially for adult learners seeking online options. Cohort Science brings analytical rigor, higher-education expertise, and missional understanding we need to ensure our new programs meet genuine student, workforce, and ministry needs. We are excited to partner together in a way that advances both our enrollment goals and our calling as a Christian university.”

The collaboration is grounded in a shared belief that evidence-based decision-making, paired with faith-driven mission, creates the most sustainable pathway for program growth. By combining rigorous analysis with a deep respect for KCU’s history, identity, and purpose, both organizations aim to position the University for long-term enrollment success and greater impact in Christian higher education.

About Cohort Science

Cohort Science specializes in analyzing longitudinal talent behavior and impact of academic offerings to generate actionable insights for colleges, universities, and organizations. With a focus on removing barriers to enrollment growth, retention, and student satisfaction, Cohort Science leverages cutting-edge machine learning and AI techniques to provide transformative solutions that drive institutional success.

title: Cohort Science Partners with Economic Mobility Systems to Evaluate Regional Talent Network Program
excerpt: [Dallas, TX] — Cohort Science announced a multiyear partnership with Economic Mobility Systems (EMS) to evaluate the Regional Talent Network (RTN) Program and generate actionable insights on implementation, efficacy, scalability, and student outcomes.
content:
Dallas, TX — March 6, 2025 — Cohort Science is thrilled to announce a new partnership with Economic Mobility Systems (EMS) for a multiyear collaboration to evaluate the Regional Talent Network (RTN) Program. This strategic initiative aims to advance postsecondary education and workforce training reforms that improve outcomes for all learners. Under the agreement, Cohort Science will evaluate the Rural Regional Talent Network (R-RTN) strategy currently implemented across three Texas regions: South Texas College, Howard College, and Odessa College. The evaluation will provide actionable insights on program implementation, efficacy, scalability, and impact on student outcomes.

“We are honored to collaborate with Economic Mobility Systems to support their noble mission of advancing equitable socioeconomic mobility,” said Raj Lalsare, Founder of Cohort Science. “Through this partnership, we are committed to delivering robust, data-driven evaluations and insights that empower educators, policymakers, and communities to create meaningful change for underserved learners.”

The R-RTN initiative emphasizes community collaboration and a redefined approach to measuring program success in rural contexts. By combining qualitative research methods—such as focus groups and stakeholder interviews—with quantitative data analysis using Salesforce and National Student Clearinghouse data, Cohort Science will ensure a comprehensive evaluation.

The evaluation will address key questions about the effectiveness and impact of the R-RTN strategy, including its ability to improve outcomes for students in the targeted regions. Findings will inform strategies for scaling and replicating successful practices, enabling broader adoption of evidence-based reforms.

Dr. Anabel Romero-Juarez, Senior Director of Regional Talent Networks at EMS, shared her enthusiasm for the partnership: “Cohort Science’s expertise in longitudinal analysis and data-driven solutions aligns perfectly with our mission. Together, we are prepared to uncover valuable insights that will help us refine and expand our efforts to create opportunities for learners across Texas.”

About Cohort Science

Cohort Science specializes in analyzing longitudinal talent behavior and impact of academic offerings to generate actionable insights for colleges, universities, and organizations. With a focus on removing barriers to enrollment growth, retention, and student satisfaction, Cohort Science leverages cutting-edge machine learning and AI techniques to provide transformative solutions that drive institutional success.
